Title: Acid Rain
Content: Acid rain comes in many forms: wet deposition, such as rain, snow, sleet, hail, and fog, and dry deposition, such as deposits of acid particles, aerosols, and gases. It is formed when sulfur dioxide (`text(SO)_2`) and nitrogen oxides (`text(NO)_text(x)`) combine with moisture in the atmosphere to produce sulfuric acid and nitric acid. Damage to aquatic and forest ecosystems, serious human illness, and the slow destruction of buildings and bridges have all been linked to acid rain.

:ibox:`text(Two)` sources that contribute to producing acid rain include:

• Emissions from airplanes, automobiles, and industries
• Emissions of `text(SO)_2` and `text(NO)_text(x)` from power plants
